title: ESPH AB Stray Dog Kennelling Services (ESPH546 JB) - AWARD
description:
The Participating Authorities (Rother District Council, Wealden District Council, Hastings Borough Council, Eastbourne Borough Council and Lewes District Council) each have a statutory duty, under the Environmental Protection Act 1990, to collect and detain stray dogs found in the District. The duty to collect dogs brought to a nominated collection point outside normal core Council opening hours was placed upon the Council under the Clean Neighbourhoods and Environment Act 2007.
      The contract covers dogs found within the whole geographic area of Rother, Wealden Hastings, Eastbourne and Lewes Councils, and therefore, providers should ensure that they are prepared to cover the service throughout the year at the rates they have.
      
      The successful tenderer will enter into three contracts with Rother District Council, Hastings Borough Council and Eastbourne Borough Council. The contract with Rother District Council will include Wealden District Council's geographic area and the contract with Eastbourne Borough Council will include Lewes District Council's geographical area.
      
      Full details are included in the tender pack.

title: ESPH CS RDC - Main Contractor for Camber Sands Welcome Centre (ESPH634) - AWARD
description:
Rother District Council (are seeking a suitably qualified and experienced Contractor to deliver the transformation of the existing visitor facilities and coastal office at Camber Car Park into a new Welcome Centre.
      
      Rother District Council has secured funding to refurbish and extend the two existing buildings at Camber car park. The works include a much-increased toilet provision and will support the running of coastal services throughout the year and particularly during the Summer season, including a larger first aid space, RNLI equipment storage and separate staffing areas for coastal staff and Operational Radcott partners. A new kiosk will offer opportunities to provide visitors with useful information, including nearby amenities and places of interest and details of local wildlife encouraging a better understanding of the unique sand dune environment.
      
      The project represents a substantial investment in visitor and community facilities by the Council. Linking the site to the wider East Sussex tourist industry including 1066 county. Accordingly, the character and quality of the proposals are intended to set a precedent and exemplar for future projects. A key focus of the grant funding and core project outcome is sustainable regeneration with these improvements core to the project brief helping Rother District Council meet its newly adopted Climate Strategy. 
      
      The Council are therefore looking for a contractor with experience of working with existing buildings in delivering low-cost, high impact refurbishments. The successful contractor will work collaboratively alongside the architects, DK-CM, to deliver a high-quality build, within the defined budget and programme.
      
      Full information is provided in the document set.

description:
Rother District Council is seeking offers to provide a Welfare Funeral Service for the Environmental Health Shared Service. The shared service is between Rother District Council and Wealden District Council.  This contract will be to provide a Welfare Funeral Service within Wealden District only.
      
      The Council carries out approximately 10 welfare funerals per year.    Section 46 of the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984 imposes a duty on the Councils to dispose of the body of any person who has died or has been found dead within its area where no suitable arrangements have been, or are being made, by anyone else. Such activity is commonly termed a welfare funeral.

title: ESPH SB RDC Architecture + Urbanism Lot 5 Further Competition - Core Design Team for De La Warr Pavilion (ESPH608 JB)
description:
Rother District Council are looking to appoint an architect as lead designer for the renovation and regenreation of the De La Warr Pavilion in Bexhill, East Sussex. 
The lead designer will be responsible for: 
- Conservation works to address all areas of deterioration identified in the condition and structural reports, and surveys.
- Building fabric works to improve long term maintenance of the Pavilion.
- Development of new environmental systems, working towards net carbon ambitions and to reduce running costs.
- Provision of improved access into and around the building for artists and audiences 
- Repairs and restoration to the South Staircase window, also addressing wider issues with metalwork and windows throughout the site.
- Building fabric repairs to the flat roof to address water ingress and resultant corrosion.
- Conservation of the entrance canopy, which suffers differential movement at the expansion joint.
- Review of external signage, which often suffers breakages.
- Restoration of the auditorium.
- Providing ancillary services to the auditorium, including cloakroom, WCs and bars.
- Upgrading backstage facilities to the auditorium, which are currently inadequate for the status of acts performing there.
- Improving visitor flow and entrance routes, particularly from the south terrace, where most visitors arrive from due to Rother District Council's substantial investment in remodelling Bexhill seafront.
- Considering gallery reconfiguration to improve visitor flow and identity of galleries.
- Developing and maximising commercial operations in Cafe, Bars, Retail and event spaces.
- Improvements to the local public realm around the Pavilion and better connection to Bexhill Town Centre.
- Development of additional footprint to accommodate desired outputs.
- Consideration and use of adjacent buildings to house DLWP facilities  
This procurement is being conducted via the Architecture and Urbanism Framework Lot 5 Civic, Cultural & Societal Infrastructure. Only suppliers registered on this Lot and expressed are invited to bid.
cpvDescriptionExpanded: Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services, Architectural and related services

title: ESPH CS RDC Construction Site Inspector (ESPH584) - AWARD
description:
The Blackfriars site in Battle has been identified in the Council's local planning documents and Corporate Plan as a site for residential development for many years. The site is approximately 16 hectares (40 acres) in size, though only around 7 hectares are considered suitable for development. Past attempts to develop the site as a whole have been unsuccessful, principally due to complex topography and ground conditions. Development of this site is predicated on the delivery of a new spine road, traversing the site from north to south which would facilitate residential development. Breheny Civil Engineering ("Breheny") have been contracted by Rother District Council ("the Council") for the delivery of the spine road which connects The Spinney and Harrier Lane.  These works have been progressing on site since April 2022.
      
      To ensure that works on the spine road are meeting technical standards of the contract the Council are seeking a Construction Site Inspector with experience in civil engineering works and working with NEC contracts.

title: Catcliffe & Treeton Flood Alleviation Scheme (Treeton Lane Bridge) - 2 Stage Pre-Construction Services and Works
description: This is a two stage design and build for Catcliffe and Treeton Flood Alleviation Shceme (Treeton lane Bridge).  The site is located South of Rotherham on B6067 Treeton Lane, Catcliffe, Rotherham, South Yorkshire. A detailed hydrological and hydraulic analysis has been undertaken and concluded the existing bridge can not accommodate the flow during flood conditions. Therefore, the freeboard and the hydraulic capacity of the bridge needed to be increased.  Based on the structural condition of the existing structure, the economic and financial feasibility of road improvements, and road capacity issues, it is proposed that the existing structure be raised by approximately 900mm at the same location over the Rother River. The preferred option would be a precast ""TY"" beam with an in-situ concrete deck slab supported by the existing abutments. However, the suitability of this option will need to be assessed as part of the Design phase.  This is a further competition via YORCivil 3 South and West Region Lot 3

title: Environmental Framework & Action Plan - Doe Lea Valley
description:
The river Doe Lea has suffered a lot with the industrial legacy of north Derbyshire & north Nottinghamshire, particularly from mining and the rapid expansion of communities to serve the mines and other industry. Significant effort has been invested in the last 40 years in cleaning up the river, but there remains a lot to do.

Through the Don, Dearne & Rother Network catchment partnership, interested parties have been meeting to share their plans and ambitions for the catchment. It is clear to these parties that there are significant opportunities for partnership working on a catchment scale to expand the scope of intervention and deliver real positive changes to the river environment and the wider catchment.

To inform the work above, the partners have secured funding through the Water Restoration Fund to develop an Environmental Framework for the Doe Lea Valley and to develop an Action Plan for the delivery of a first trial phase. On behalf of the partners, the Chesterfield Canal Trust is now seeking consultants to deliver this work.

Further work may be commissioned at a later date to monitor and evaluate the success of interventions and to refine and develop the Action Plan for future phases, subject to future funding and endorsement by the partners.

The details of this phase of the work and the tender administration process are set out in full in the attached Project Brief, or by contacting the Chesterfield Canal Trust Development Manager, George Rogers, development@chesterfield-canal-trust.org.uk

title: ESPH AB HBC Accommodate and Connect - Immediate accommodation of rough sleepers (MP063 JB) - AWARD
description:
Hastings Borough Council, leading and in partnership with Eastbourne, Lewes, Rother, and Wealden Councils, have been successfully awarded the contract for the delivery of a new test and learn project funded by the Centre for Homelessness Impact, Accommodate and Connect. 
      
      The project aims to remove the barriers that vulnerable people who are having to sleep rough face, when accessing accommodation in the area they are presenting in. As such, the project aims to support local authorities to deliver a range of immediate, short-term emergency or off-the-street (OTS) accommodation options that can be used to help those presenting as rough sleeping without local connection. They will benefit from access to wrap around support to explore a reconnection back to their original area of residence and source long-term accommodation to end their rough sleeping and/or homelessness. The project also aims to help support those eligible with local accommodation options where a reconnection is not attainable. 
      
      Full details are included in the document set.
